title: Trump Backs Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Despite Midterm Defeat Driven by Iran War
snippet: President Donald Trump affirmed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth will remain in his role following sweeping Republican midterm losses attributed to the ongoing conflict with Iran.
content:
WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump firmly backed Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday, dismissing speculation of a leadership shakeup at the Pentagon following a brutal midterm election cycle for Republicans that party leaders largely blamed on the military conflict with Iran.

Addressing reporters, Trump brushed off rumors that Hegseth might be replaced or transition to run for Tennessee's open U.S. Senate seat, declaring that the Pentagon chief was "doing a great job." The Senate seat is opening up after Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn won the state's gubernatorial race on Tuesday. Blackburn declined to comment on potential appointees to her seat.

Fallout from a Costly Conflict

The political maneuvering follows severe midterm losses for Republicans, driven by public frustration over an eight-month war that has pushed up gas prices and drained U.S. munitions reserves. Exit polling indicated that 34% of voters viewed the Iran conflict as crucial to their decision, while nearly half cited the cost of living.

Even within the administration, friction over the war has spilled into the open. Vice President JD Vance issued a candid rebuke on social media Wednesday, directly connecting the election results to the administration's foreign policy. "The reason we lost is the war," Vance wrote, urging the party to acknowledge the political price paid at the ballot box.

Democratic Oversight Looming

With Democrats preparing to take over majorities in Congress, the Pentagon is braced for intense scrutiny. Incoming committee leaders have signaled plans to use subpoena power to probe Hegseth's handling of the war, his adherence to War Powers deadlines, and recent high-profile firings of senior military officials.

However, the Pentagon pushed back aggressively against rumors of Hegseth's departure. Department spokesperson Sean Parnell insisted Hegseth remains "100% committed to leading the Department until the end of President Trump's term in office," asserting that the defense secretary will not be deterred by political oversight.
